triple.subject: Track A / Track B
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: Track A refers to head-weighted benchmark metrics (per-item accuracy, per-turn preference) that remain stable or rise during collapse; Track B refers to tail-sensitive diagnostic measures that detect collapse earlier.

triple.subject: distinction sensitivity (D)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A reference-free collapse measure computed as the ratio of semantic distance between a model's answers to a meaning-altering variant versus a meaning-preserving paraphrase; D ≫ 1 indicates intact distinctions, D → 1 indicates collapse.

triple.subject: effective modes (N_eff)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A measure of semantic diversity across a model's sampled outputs for a given probe, computed via entropy over meaning-cluster mass or the Vendi score, capturing collapse when surface variety masks a shrinking set of distinct meanings.

triple.subject: cross-prompt convergence (X)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A diagnostic measuring the mean pairwise distance between embedding centroids of a model's outputs across semantically unrelated prompts; X falling indicates diverse inputs are being forced through one representational channel.

triple.subject: self-consumption contraction (λ)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: The estimated derivative of the collapse map at one generation — the dispersion ratio of output variance after a model is conditioned on or fine-tuned on its own samples — used to compute generations-to-halve as log 0.5 / log λ.

triple.subject: MCSD_t (Model Collapse Self-Diagnostic index)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A geometric composite index combining ratios of distinction sensitivity, effective modes, cross-prompt spread, Gini concentration, and contraction relative to a prior snapshot, ranging from 0 (no detected contraction) to 1 (maximal measured).

triple.subject: collapsed-prediction ratio
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: The fraction of generation steps at which the top-token probability p_top ≥ 0.999, used as a Gambetta-panel indicator of next-token mass concentration and late-stage collapse.

triple.subject: surplexity
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: The surprise of a training document under the model being trained; a falling surplexity slope indicates the model is being trained on increasingly low-surprise documents, which the Gambetta et al. work identifies as a leading indicator of collapse.

triple.subject: composition audit
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A procedure for ranking each probe's tokens against a declared open-corpus frequency ranking to report a benchmark suite's head/mid/tail weighting and the predicted detection lag, exposing systematic bias toward head-band items.

triple.subject: the gate rule
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A proposed training governance rule under which a checkpoint is admitted to further training only if the Part II collapse panel does not move in the collapse direction past declared thresholds relative to the prior checkpoint.

triple.subject: three conditions (base / instruction-tuned / production scaffold)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A control structure requiring that all collapse measures be computed three times — at bare prompt, instruction interface, and full production scaffold — so that interface-induced contraction can be separated from training-loop collapse.

triple.subject: representational collapse (effective rank R_eff)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A white-box collapse measure computed as the participation ratio of covariance eigenvalues of hidden states, falling when more distinct inputs are represented in fewer effective dimensions.

triple.subject: Reader's Test (Part III)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A text-only, reference-free self-diagnostic protocol for a language model reading the deposit, measuring distinction sensitivity, effective modes, cross-prompt convergence, and self-conditioning contraction using only the model's own constructions.

triple.subject: canary (collapse proxy)
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A technique for estimating self-consumption contraction when the primary model cannot be fine-tuned: a small proxy model is trained on the primary model's samples and its collapse panel is measured, reading the data's collapse potential.

triple.subject: mixture ledger
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A required disclosure component of the diagnostic publication, tracking synthetic data share, mediated share, and the human-data admission weight w_H across training rounds, providing causal context for panel readings.

triple.subject: detection lag
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: The number of training generations between the onset of collapse and its detection by a given benchmark composition, shown to be monotonically increasing in head-weighting of the probe set.

triple.subject: interlocking autoregression
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A companion theoretical toy (deposit #1556) modelling the training ecology as X_{n+1} = F(X_n; I, II, III), Y_n = M_IV(X_n), demonstrating that the certification instruments measure a unit orthogonal to the state variable.

triple.subject: head/mid/tail band
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A tripartite classification of benchmark probe tokens by corpus frequency rank — head (high-frequency), mid (medium), tail (low-frequency) — used to assess probe composition and predict detection lag.

triple.subject: mediation ratchet
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A component of the companion model (Component II) describing how the deployment scaffold or instruction interface induces and accumulates diversity contraction independently of training-loop collapse.

triple.subject: two-track reporting
triple.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
triple.note: A proposed benchmark reporting standard requiring that every Track A (head-weighted accuracy) score carry a simultaneous Part II collapse-panel reading on the same checkpoint.
